name: K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' founds Copán
traveler: K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo', 'Sun-eyed Green Quetzal Macaw'
summary: Altar Q at Copán, carved 350 years later, tells how the dynasty began. In September 426 a lord named K'uk' Mo' took the emblems of kingship at the Wiinte' Naah, a fire shrine tied to Teotihuacan, and 152 days later he arrived at Copán to found a line of sixteen kings. The strontium in his teeth, found in the tomb beneath the Acropolis, says he grew up in the central Petén, perhaps at Tikal; his portraits wear Teotihuacan's goggles. Where the Wiinte' Naah stood is still argued.

stops.note: Isotopes in his teeth point to a childhood in the central Petén, in Tikal's orbit after Teotihuacan's 'arrival' of 378.

stops.place: The Wiinte' Naah, perhaps at Teotihuacan
stops.note: On 5 September 426 he 'takes the k'awiil', the sceptre of kingship, at a 'root-house' tied to Teotihuacan's fire cult.
'He arrives' 152 days later, on 9 February 427, and is remembered as 'the lord of the west'. His tomb lies deep beneath Temple 16.
